Order : (Per Smt.Meena Ramanathan, Hon'ble I/c President)
[
1. This is an appeal filed by the Appellants/Opposite Parties
under
Section-15
of Consumer Protection Act, 1986, R/w.
Section-
41
of Consumer Protection Act, 2019, against the order dated
18.11.2021 of the District Consumer Commission, Adilabad made
in C.C.No.187/2018. The Appellant is the Opposite Party No.2,
Respondent No.1 is the Complainant, Respondent No.2, 3 and 4
are the Opposite Party No.1, 3 and 4 in CC.No.187/2018.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are described as
arrayed in the complaint.
3. The facts of the complaint are that the Complainant is a
resident of Nirmal District and booked her flight tickets to travel to
Tirupathi from Hyderabad. Onward journey was booked for travel
to Tirupathi on 01.06.2016 and return on 04.06.2016. The tickets
were booked through Opposite Party No.1 & 2 and the airline is
Opposite Party No.3. The Complainant insured the journey with
Opposite Party No.4-Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company
Limited. The Policy vide No.OG-17-1901-9905-00001178 was valid
for the period 01.06.2016 to 30.06.2016 for a premium of
Rs.100/-.
4. It is the Complainant's grievance that Opposite Party No.3
intimated her on 31.05.2016 at 14:00 hours about the flight
cancellation when arrangements were already made at Tirupathi
for the hotel accommodation and other arrangements for seeing
the nearby temples. Moreover, the Complainant had already
proceeded to Hyderabad by a hire vehicle prior to the intimation
3
from Opposite Party No.3. The loss incurred has been immense
and non-attendance at Tirupathi for Darshan has caused the
Complainant much distress and agony. The present complaint is
raised against the Opposite Parties for their deficiency in service
and failure to respond to the several requests raised by the
Complainant for compensation and costs.
5. The Opposite Party No.1 failed to appear and was set
exparte. The Opposite Party No.2 filed their written version stating
that it is a travel agency with a wide base in more than 60
locations across India, USA and Canada. The Complainant
approached Opposite Party No.1, who is an agent of Opposite Party
No.2 to avail the service of booking flight tickets from Hyderabad to
Tirupathi on 01.06.2016 and return on 04.06.2016 along with
hotel rooms for the duration of her stay.
6. On 31.05.2016, Opposite Party No.3 informed Opposite Party
No.2 about the cancellation of flight and the information was
passed on to the Complainant through Opposite Party No.1. The
Opposite Party No.3 refunded the cost of flight tickets which were
promptly paid to the Complainant.
7. The Complainant is demanding refund of hotel booking,
darshan tickets and cab services from Opposite Party No.2 which
were done subject to terms and conditions of respective operators,
therefore, this Opposite Party No.2 is in no way concerned with the
allegations and reliefs claimed by the Complainant. All the reliefs
and damages are directly attributable to the cancellation of the
flight, hence they seek dismissal of the complaint against this
Opposite Party with costs.
8. The Opposite Party No.3 was set exparte. The Opposite Party
No.4 is the Insurance Company and as per their written version
the flight was cancelled by the Airlines-Opposite Party No.3 and
the amount was refunded to the Complainant. As per their policy
terms and conditions Section VIII reads as follows:-
4
Section VIII: Trip Cancellation:
"Subject to all other terms and conditions, the company will
indemnify the insured subject to limits shown in schedule, for loss of
ticket charges paid or contracted to be paid by the insured, which
are not recoverable from any other source."
9. In this case, Opposite Party No.3 has refunded the ticket
amount to the Complainant, therefore, the Complainant is not
liable for any compensation from this Opposite Party No.4 the
Insurance Company. The Complainant is taking a chance litigation
and in view of the facts and circumstances, they seek dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
10. Before the District Commission, the Complainant filed
Evidence Affidavit and got marked Ex.A1 to A3. The Opposite Party
No.4 filed evidence affidavit. Ex.B1 & B2 are marked on their
behalf.
11. The District Commission after hearing and considering the
material on record, allowed the complaint directing the Opposite
Party No.1 to 3 to pay each Rs.50,000/- in all with interest @ 12%
p.a. from the date of cancellation of flight ticket till realization. The
Opposite Party No.4 is directed to pay Rs.10,000/- with interest @
18% p.a. from the date of complaint till realization. No costs,
compliance within (4) weeks from the date of receipt of the order.
12. Aggrieved by the order of the District Commission, the
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 preferred this appeal with the
following grounds:
 The District Forum grossly erred in holding that alternative
 arrangements were not done by the Opposite Parties. The
 alternative arrangements had to be done by Opposite Party
 No.3/Airlines but not by Appellant.
 The District Forum failed to consider that the Appellant is
 only facilitator and neither it had control nor operation of
 flight and cancellation.
5
 The District Forum failed to consider that the ticket amounts
 were refunded to Respondent No.1/Complainant.
  The District Forum failed to appreciate that the hotel rooms
 were booked through cleartrip.com and as per terms, if the
 person does not arrive on the first night of accommodation
 booked, the property will be released and they will be
 charged full. Hence, there is no role of Appellant in refund of
 hotel charges.
 The District Forum ought not to have held that there is a
 deficiency of service and unfair trade practice on the part of
 the Appellant without recording any reason for such
 conclusion.
13. The point that arises for consideration is whether the
impugned order as passed by the District Forum suffers from any
error or irregularity or whether it is liable to be set aside, modified
or interfered with, in any manner? To what relief?
14. We have perused the material available on record and heard
the counsel for the parties. On perusal of the record, we find that
Opposite Party No.3-Airlines was set exparte in the
CC.No.187/2018 on the file of District Commission, Adilabad,
however vide IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 they filed their
written arguments in order to participate in the proceedings before
this Commission. Since the impugned order imposed liability on
the Opposite Party No.3 who were set exparte in the Commission
below, we find it necessary to consider their arguments to provide
justice to both parties. The written arguments filed vide
IA.No.78/2022 in FA.No.22/2022 is common to all the appeals of
this batch and the same is thus considered.
15. The Opposite Party No.3 filed its written arguments which we
have considered for the reason that they were also made liable to
compensate the Respondent/Complainant by the Commission
6
below. The sum and substance of their submission in brief is as
follows:
The Opposite Party No.3 published their conditions on their
website and these conditions govern the journey and rights of the
passengers who opt to book flight tickets either from the website or
through travel agents. As per the provisions of carriage by
Air Act
,
the generated tickets shall be treated as contract of carriage and
these conditions constitute a valid binding contract between
parties. The Complainant having accepted the full refund cannot
now allege deficiency in service and therefore, prayed dismissal of
the complaint in the interest of justice.
16. The brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present
complaint are that the Respondent No.1/Complainant booked
flight tickets as follows:
01.06.2016 - Onward Journey from Hyderabad to Tirupathi
04.06.2016 - Return Journey from Tirupathi to Hyderabad

Tickets were booked on 17.05.2016 through travel agent Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 in the main complaint.
17. The present appeal is only preferred by Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2. The Respondent No.4/Opposite Party No.4 is the
General Insurance Company engaged in the business of general
insurance including Air Travel Insurance in collaboration with
Respondent No.3/Opposite Party No.3.
18. Since the flight was cancelled, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant requested the Opposite Parties to arrange
alternate arrangements as they were on their way to Hyderabad
and the schedule was booked in advance for Darshan at Tirupathi
and accommodation at hotels in various places of pilgrimage. Due
to the sudden cancellation of the flight, the Respondent
No.1/Complainant incurred a heavy loss and suffered great
7
hardship and therefore, repeatedly requested the Respondent No.2
to 4 i.e., Opposite Parties 1, 3 and 4 to settle the matter.
19. The main controversy that requires our attention is, when
the flight is suddenly cancelled, who is responsible for the
connected expenses of having booked the hotel rooms, paid for a
darshan at Tirupathi and vehicle expenditure?
20. The fact that the flight tickets were cancelled on the day
before date of travel is not in dispute. The Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 herein has admitted in their written version that
Opposite Party No.1 is their agent and that the Respondent
No.1/Complainant booked the tickets to Tirupathi and the return
to Hyderabad through Opposite Party No.1. It is also admitted that
Opposite Party No.1 booked the hotel accommodation at Hotel SLV
Grand for their stay from 01.06.2016 to 03.06.2016. When
Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 was informed about the flight
cancellation, it is the duty of the travel agent to immediately inform
his customers and also inform the hotel about the change in
itinerary. Merely stating that the cost of flight tickets has been
refunded is not sufficient to escape from their responsibility with
regard to the hotel accommodation expenses paid by the
Respondent No.1/Complainant.
21. The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 cannot escape from his
liability by stating that they are only facilitators and that booking
of hotel accommodation was subject to terms and conditions of
respective operators. Who are the respective operators? Opposite
Party No.1 and 2 are the respective operators and must invariably
be held accountable for the cancellation of the hotel rooms at
Tirupathi and elsewhere since the Respondent No.1/Complainant
could not undertake the journey owing to the flight being suddenly
cancelled.
8
22. The impugned order needlessly directed Opposite Party No.1
to 3 to compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant. The cost of
tickets was already refunded to the Respondent No.1/Complainant
as evidenced vide Ex.A5. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. A thorough scrutiny of this exhibit reveals that the
said journey was planned by a family of 18 members and they had
all travelled from Nirmal District to Hyderabad on the previous day
in order to board the flight on 01.06.2016 at Hyderabad to
Tirupathi. The sudden cancellation of the flight is neither their
fault nor the fault of the tour operator-Opposite Party No.2, but
having made all their arrangements at Tirupathi, it is the burden
of Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 to reimburse the monies spent
towards the hotel accommodation to the Complainant/s.
23. The Respondent/Opposite Party No.4/Insurance Company
has no role to play in this controversy since the policy in question
is with regard to indemnifying the insured for loss of ticket charges
due to unavoidable cancellation of the trip because of death,
sudden injury or sickness requiring hospitalization. Since the
Airline cancelled the flight and the cost of tickets was refunded to
the Respondent No.1/Complainant, Opposite Party No.4 is not
held responsible and only Opposite Party No.2 is directed to
compensate the Respondent No.1/Complainant for the loss and
damages incurred.
24. The Commission below has without any material evidence
concluded that the Opposite Party No.1 to 3 must pay an amount
of Rs.50,000/- to each Complainant along with interest and
Opposite Party No.4 is further directed to pay Rs.10,000/- along
with interest from the date of complaint till realization. This
direction cannot be sustained for the simple reason that the
Respondent No.1/Complainant has failed to prove that he/she has
spent money towards the hotel accommodation. The only receipts
that are filed are Ex.A3 for a sum of Rs.2,100/- being the TTD
Special Entry Darshan Receipt. This receipt clearly reveals that
ticket cost per person is only Rs.300/-, therefore, this Ex.A3 is the
9
ticket for 7 persons. Although this exhibit is not filed in all the
appeals concerning this batch, the same is being considered as
common to all. Besides this, the Respondent No.1/Complainant
would have incurred an additional expenditure of travelling to
Hyderabad from Nirmal District to board the flight.
25. Hence, keeping all these aspects in mind, we consider
granting a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards compensation as fair and
just. The cost of flight tickets has been refunded to the
Respondent No.1/Complainant and this was erroneously over-
looked by the Commission below. Although the
Respondent/Opposite Party No.4 has not preferred an appeal
challenging the impugned order, we consider imposing liability on
them as unjustified in view of the policy conditions which were not
adverted to by the Commission below.
26. For the reasons stated herein above and after giving
thoughtful consideration to the entire facts and circumstances of
the case, the appeal is liable to be dismissed by modifying the
impugned order.
27. In the result, the appeal is disposed of by modifying the
impugned order and the following direction is passed in its place:
The Appellant/Opposite Party No.2 is directed to pay the
Respondent No.1/Complainant a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards
compensation. Time for compliance is six weeks, failing which the
amount of Rs.10,000/- shall carry interest @ 8% p.a. till
realization. The parties to bear their own costs.
Sd/- Sd/-
 I/C PRESIDENT MEMBER-J
 Dt: 07.12.2023
 UC*
